passages.text: The following discussion analyzes our financial condition and results of operations and should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, wherein WES Operating is fully consolidated, and which are included under Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K, and the information set forth in Risk Factors under Part I, Item 1A of this Form 10-K. Discussion of 2023 items, and comparison of the year ended December 31, 2024, to the year ended December 31, 2023, that are not included in this annual report on Form 10-K can be found under Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, which is included under Part II, Item 7 of our annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, as filed with the SEC on February 26, 2025, and is available via the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov and our website at www.westernmidstream.com. The Partnership’s assets include assets owned and ownership interests accounted for by us under the equity method of accounting, through our 98.1% partnership interest in WES Operating, as of December 31, 2025. Amounts attributable to noncontrolling interests presented in this Item 7 consist of (i) the 25% third-party interest in Chipeta for all periods presented, and only for natural-gas assets for throughput attributable to WES, and (ii) the 1.9%, 2.0%, and 2.0% limited partner interest in WES Operating as of December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively, owned by an Occidental subsidiary. See Note 1—Summary of Significant Accounting Policies and Basis of Presentation and Note 7—Equity Investments in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements under Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K. We also own and control the entire non-economic general partner interest in WES Operating GP, and our general partner is owned by Occidental. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY We are a midstream energy company organized as a publicly traded partnership, engaged in the business of gathering, compressing, treating, processing, and transporting natural gas; gathering, stabilizing, and transporting condensate, NGLs, and crude oil; and gathering, transporting, recycling, treating, supplying, and disposing of produced water. In our capacity as a natural - gas processor, we also buy and sell residue, NGLs, and condensate on behalf of ourselves and our customers under certain contracts. To provide superior midstream service, we focus on ensuring the reliability and performance of our systems, creating sustainable cost efficiencies, enhancing our safety culture, and protecting the environment. We own or have investments in assets located in Texas, New Mexico, and the Rocky Mountains (Colorado, Utah, and Wyoming). As of December 31, 2025, WES Operating had (i) no outstanding borrowings under the RCF that bear interest at a rate based on the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (“SOFR”) or an alternative base rate at WES Operating’s option and (ii) no outstanding commercial paper borrowings. While a 10% change in the applicable benchmark interest rate would not materially impact interest expense on our outstanding borrowings at December 31, 2025, it would impact the fair value of the senior notes. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin is well above the sector median, reflecting the fee-based gathering, processing and treating mix across Texas, New Mexico and the Rockies, where contract structures limit direct commodity exposure. This supports relatively stable EBITDA through the cycle and underpins the issuer's capacity to service a large senior note stack.

Gross and net leverage sit comfortably below the sector median, and net leverage remains inside the next risk-band boundary, leaving meaningful headroom before a downgrade trigger. The partnership's scale and unsecured curve compare favourably with weaker midstream peers on the same definition.

key_risks.text: Leverage has risen year over year as debt increased while operating income fell, so the favourable comparison versus peers partly reflects a softer comparative base. Continued debt-funded growth or weaker gathering volumes would erode the current cushion toward the next risk-band boundary, which is the key sensitivity for the indicative profile.

The debt note shows a large unsecured senior note stack with near-term maturities, including notes due in the coming year, and the borrower is WES Operating rather than the parent. Refinancing depends on continued access to unsecured markets, and the disclosed interest-rate risk factor flags sensitivity of note fair values to benchmark moves.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is above the sector median and comfortably above unity, with operating income covering gross interest expense several times over. Coverage nonetheless declined year over year as interest expense grew alongside the larger debt balance, so the trend direction is negative even though the absolute level remains adequate.

Operating cash flow covers distributions with a modest margin, and cash flow to debt exceeds the sector median and the next risk-band boundary. However, free cash flow and capex are not determinable from the bundle, so the true call on cash after growth investment and distributions cannot be assessed.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is Significant, driven by leverage and cash-flow tiers that sit below sector medians but above the upgrade thresholds. Liquidity is adequate, with a current ratio above both the prior year and the sector median, and no commercial paper or revolver drawings outstanding at year end.

Our judgement is a stable but trend-sensitive credit: strong margins and above-peer coverage support the senior unsecured notes, while rising leverage, near-term maturities and distributions absorbing most operating cash flow constrain upside. Missing capex prevents a full free-cash-flow view, which we treat as a material gap for the servicing assessment.

credit_strengths.text: 營運利潤率遠高於行業中位數，反映橫跨德州、新墨西哥州及洛磯山脈地區以收費為基礎的集氣、處理及加工業務組合，其合約結構限制了直接商品價格曝險。此支撐整個週期內相對穩定的 EBITDA，並奠定發行人償付大額優先票據的能力。
總槓桿及淨槓桿均舒適地低於行業中位數，淨槓桿仍處於下一個風險區間邊界之內，在觸發降級前留有顯著緩衝。合夥企業的規模及無擔保曲線，按同一界定與較弱的中游同業相比更為有利。

key_risks.text: 槓桿按年上升，因債務增加而營運收入下降，故與同業相比的有利表現部分反映比較基數較弱。持續以債務融資的增長或集氣量轉弱，將侵蝕當前緩衝並趨向下一風險區間邊界，此為指示性評級輪廓的關鍵敏感因素。
債務說明顯示大額無擔保優先票據，且近期到期，包括來年到期票據，而借款人為 WES Operating 而非母公司。再融資取決於能否持續進入無擔保市場，而披露的利率風險因素指出票據公允價值對基準利率變動的敏感度。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率高于行業中位數，並舒適地高於一，營運收入覆蓋總利息支出數倍以上。然而，覆蓋率按年下降，因利息支出隨較大債務餘額增加，故趨勢方向為負面，儘管絕對水平仍屬足夠。
營運現金流以溫和幅度覆蓋分派，現金流對債務比率高於行業中位數及下一風險區間邊界。然而，自由現金流及資本開支無法從資料組合中確定，故增長投資及分派後的實際現金需求無法評估。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險輪廓為顯著，由槓桿及現金流層級驅動，兩者低於行業中位數但高於升級門檻。流動性足夠，流動比率高於去年及行業中位數，且年末並無未償還商業票據或循環信貸提取。
我們的判斷為穩定但對趨勢敏感的信用：強勁利潤率及高於同業的覆蓋率支撐優先無擔保票據，而槓桿上升、近期到期及分派吸收大部分營運現金流則限制上行空間。資本開支缺失妨礙全面自由現金流觀點，我們視此為償債評估的重大缺口。
